Control your car over Bluetooth
This app talks directly to your car with Tesla\'s secure Bluetooth protocol. No internet connection or Tesla account is needed. Setup takes about five minutes, and one step needs you in the car.

Your car
Enter the 17-character VIN (Vehicle Identification Number).
Quickest: in the Tesla app, touch and hold the VIN at the bottom of the car\'s main screen to copy it, then come back and tap “Paste VIN”.
You can also find it on the car\'s touchscreen (Controls, then Software), through the windshield at the bottom corner on the driver\'s side, or on the label in the driver\'s door frame.

Android will ask for two permissions.

• Nearby devices lets the app find and connect to your car.

• Location is required by Android for any Bluetooth scan. Choose “Precise”. The app only uses it to find your car.

Location also needs to be switched on the first time the app looks for your car.

Choose access
Choose what this phone may do. You can pair again later to change it.

Owner
Full control, including adding and removing keys and changing PINs. Recommended for your own car.
Driver
Everything except managing keys and PINs. Good for a family member\'s phone.
Approve with your key card
1. Sit in the car with your key card. If your phone is on the wireless charger, take it off.
2. Tap “Send pairing request”.
3. Right away, place the key card flat on the card reader and hold it still for a few seconds.
The car\'s screen may not show anything. That\'s normal: this app notices the approval by itself.
Where the card reader is
Model 3 from 2024: on the wireless phone charger.
Earlier Model 3, and Model Y: on the centre console, just behind the cup holders.
Model S, Model X and Cybertruck: if one spot doesn\'t react, try the other.
A key card placed on the wireless phone charger at the front of the centre console.
A key card placed on the centre console just behind the cup holders.

Nothing happening? Try the other spot: the wireless phone charger, or just behind the cup holders. Keep the card still for a few seconds, with no phone on top of it.
Approved. This phone is now a key.
No approval yet. Send the request again, then place the key card on the reader straight away.

Troubleshooting
The app can\'t find my car
Stand within a few metres of the car. Bluetooth range is short, especially through walls.
Check the VIN in Settings, then Cars. One wrong character makes the app look for a different car.
Make sure Bluetooth is on, and location too for the first search.
Open a door to wake the car, then try again.
The car already has 3 Bluetooth connections
The car keeps at most three Bluetooth connections, shared by key fobs and phone keys.
Move other phones that are keys for this car away (or close their Tesla app), then try again.
A car connected to three devices, with a fourth phone refused.
Pairing doesn\'t finish
The car\'s screen often shows nothing while pairing. Place the key card on the reader right after you send the request.
Model 3 from 2024 reads the card on the wireless phone charger. Earlier Model 3 and Model Y read it just behind the cup holders. Not sure? Try both.
Take your phone off the charger first. Tesla warns that a phone and a card on the charger together can damage the card.
If the car has many keys, remove an old one first, from Security, then Keys, or on the car\'s Locks screen.
It says this phone isn\'t paired
The key may have been removed on the car\'s Locks screen, or the app was reinstalled, which creates a new key.
Run the setup guide again and approve with your key card.
Remove the old phone key on the car\'s Locks screen to keep the list tidy.
The car is asleep, slow, or numbers are missing
Locks, trunk and frunk work while the car sleeps.
Climate, charging and media need the car awake. The app wakes it automatically (Settings, then “Wake the car automatically”). Waking can take up to 30 seconds.
Battery and climate readings appear once the car is awake. The app doesn\'t wake the car just to read them, to save its battery.
A sleeping car.
Bluetooth is off or a permission was denied
Turn on Bluetooth from Quick Settings.
If you denied a permission, open the phone\'s Settings, then Apps, then Tesla BLE Control, then Permissions, and allow Nearby devices and Location.
Location must be on for the first search. After that the app connects to the remembered car without it.
The Bluetooth symbol crossed out.
Using the app with several cars
Add each car in Settings, then Cars, then “Add another car”, and pair it once with its key card.
Switch cars with the car name at the top of every screen.
This phone uses the same key for every car it is paired with.
